original_question: Find local matching rules for quasicrystal tilings in dimension 2 or 3 such that both of the following hold. First, for every tile type t and every finite region R made of tiles, the discrepancy D_t(R)=|N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| is bounded by c_t |∂R| for some constant c_t depending only on t, where N_t(R) counts tiles of type t in R and d(t) is the density of t. Second, the same perimeter-order discrepancy bound holds for every pattern or patch that satisfies the matching rules.
target_in_paper: Problem 2.7.3 in Section 2.7.2, "Modelling Physical Phenomena with Quasicrystals (After J. Miękisz)": "Find a set of matching rules in dimension 2 and/or 3 that meet both condition (A) and condition (B)." ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official target very closely: it asks for matching rules in dimension 2 or 3, states condition (A) with the same discrepancy formula and perimeter-order bound, and includes condition (B) for admissible patterns or patches. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
missing_details: The paper asks for the existence of a set of local matching rules used to define a tiling, not for a classification of all such rules. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

The region R should be specified as a region of an admissible tiling that is a finite union of tiles; vol(R) is its Euclidean area/volume and |∂R| is the measure of its boundary. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should state that the relevant densities exist. The paper notes that if the system is not uniquely ergodic, fluctuations are volume-order rather than perimeter-order, so the problem is only meaningful when density is well-defined. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

Condition (B) needs an explicit patch-level analogue of condition (A): for each admissible finite patch P, one must specify what N_P(R) counts (occurrences of P contained in R) and what its density d(P) means. The paper states this tersely as "property (A) should also hold for any pattern or patch satisfying the given matching rule." ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

The neighboring Problem 2.7.4 is only a first-step variant asking for condition (A) alone in dimension 2; the paper also remarks that a dimension-3 analogue of Problem 2.7.4 is available, while known 2D examples such as Penrose have discrepancy O(|∂R| log |∂R|). This context should not be folded into the main question, but it explains the scope. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

Not applicable here: the paper involves no ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity or degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or "for all sufficiently large m" clause; the missing items are geometric quantifiers, admissibility conventions, and density assumptions. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
refined_question: Find a local set of matching rules for tilings of R^2 or R^3 such that, for every admissible tiling defined by those rules, every tile type t has a well-defined density d(t) and satisfies the low-fluctuation estimate |N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| <= c_t|∂R| for every region R that is a finite union of tiles, where c_t depends only on t; and such that, for every admissible finite patch P satisfying the same rules, the analogous discrepancy bound |N_P(R)-d(P)vol(R)| <= c_P|∂R| holds for every such region R, where N_P(R) counts occurrences of P wholly contained in R, d(P) is the density of P, vol(R) is Euclidean area/volume, and |∂R| is boundary measure. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
justification: This reformulation stays closest to the paper because the exact target is the existence problem in Problem 2.7.3, stated immediately after conditions (A) and (B) in §2.7.2. The nearby remarks supply the hidden assumptions your draft leaves implicit: density is only meaningful in the relevant uniquely ergodic setting, condition (B) is the real extra difficulty, and Problem 2.7.4 is explicitly presented only as a first step toward Problem 2.7.3. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
